name: Jeera Rice
cuisine: North Indian (Punjabi dhaba and restaurant staple, cooked at home across India)

ingredients.name: Basmati rice
ingredients.householdMeasure: A little over ⅓ cup (⅓ cup + 1 tbsp)

ingredients.name: Water (for cooking)
ingredients.householdMeasure: About ¾ cup (open pan) / about ⅔ cup (cooker)

equipment: Small heavy-bottomed saucepan (1–1.5 litre) with a tight-fitting lid (open-pan method)
OR a 2–3 litre pressure cooker (pressure-cooker method)
Mixing bowl for rinsing and soaking
Sieve or strainer for draining the soaked rice
Measuring cup and spoons (a standard steel tumbler and ordinary teaspoons are fine stand-ins; use the same cup for rice and water)
Spatula or flat spoon; a fork for fluffing
Chopping board and knife (for the chilli and coriander)

steps.title: Measure the rice
steps.text: Measure 75 g basmati rice (⅓ cup + 1 tbsp) into the bowl.
steps.tip: Spread it on a plate first and pick out any small stones or dark grains.
steps.visualCue: Long white grains, no stones or husks
steps.cameraCheck: The measured rice in the bowl
steps.videoShot: Rice pouring from the cup into the bowl.

steps.title: Rinse the rice
steps.text: Add water to cover, swirl gently with your fingers, and pour the cloudy water away. Repeat 3–4 times.
steps.tip: Swirl, do not rub hard. Basmati grains are long and break easily.
steps.visualCue: The water is almost clear on the last rinse.
steps.cameraCheck: The bowl of rice in nearly clear water
steps.videoShot: Fingers swirling the rice, cloudy water draining off.

steps.title: Soak the rice
steps.text: Cover the rinsed rice with about 1 cup fresh water and leave it for 20 minutes.
steps.tip: In a hurry? Soak 10 min and add 1 extra tbsp of water when cooking. Do the next steps (chopping) while it soaks.
steps.visualCue: The grains turn opaque white and slightly plumper.
steps.cameraCheck: The rice soaking in the bowl
steps.videoShot: A still shot of soaking rice, then a timer set to 20 min.

steps.title: Chop the coriander
steps.text: Finely chop 3 g (2 tsp) coriander leaves. Keep aside.
steps.visualCue: Fine green flecks
steps.cameraCheck: 2 tsp chopped coriander
steps.videoShot: The knife rocking through coriander.

steps.title: Slit the green chilli (optional)
steps.text: Slit ½ green chilli lengthwise, keeping it in one piece.
steps.tip: Leaving it whole gives aroma with mild heat; you can pick it out before serving.
steps.visualCue: A chilli half split open, seeds showing
steps.cameraCheck: The slit chilli on the board
steps.videoShot: The knife tip running down the chilli.

steps.title: Measure the cooking water
steps.text: Measure 170 ml (about ¾ cup) water and keep it near the stove.
steps.tip: This is about 1¾ times the volume of the dry rice, the ratio most sources use for soaked basmati in an open pan.
steps.visualCue: Water at the ¾-cup line
steps.cameraCheck: The measuring cup of water
steps.videoShot: Water poured into the measuring cup.

steps.title: Drain the rice
steps.text: Pour the soaked rice into the sieve and let it drip.
steps.visualCue: No water dripping from the sieve
steps.cameraCheck: The drained rice in the sieve
steps.videoShot: Water running out of the sieve.

steps.title: Heat the ghee
steps.text: Put the saucepan on medium heat and add 1½ tsp (7 g) ghee.
steps.visualCue: The ghee melts and turns clear with a light shimmer, no smoke.
steps.cameraCheck: Melted ghee in the pan
steps.videoShot: The ghee melting and spreading across the pan.

steps.title: Add the cumin seeds
steps.text: Add 1 tsp (2 g) cumin seeds.
steps.tip: If the ghee is not hot enough, the seeds will not sizzle. If they turn black, they are burnt and bitter: wipe the pan and start again.
steps.visualCue: The seeds sizzle and crackle, turn one shade darker, and smell nutty.
steps.cameraCheck: Sizzling cumin in the ghee
steps.videoShot: Cumin hitting the hot ghee and fizzing.

steps.title: Add the whole spices
steps.text: Add the bay leaf, the cracked cardamom pod and 2 cloves. Stir once.
steps.visualCue: The bay leaf darkens slightly and the cloves puff a little; a warm, sweet smell rises.
steps.cameraCheck: The spices in the ghee
steps.videoShot: Bay leaf and cloves dropping into the pan.

steps.title: Add the green chilli
steps.text: Add the slit chilli. Stir for a few seconds.
steps.visualCue: The chilli skin blisters lightly.
steps.cameraCheck: The chilli in the tempering
steps.videoShot: The chilli sizzling.

steps.title: Add the drained rice
steps.text: Tip the drained rice into the pan.
steps.visualCue: The rice sits on top of the spices and ghee.
steps.cameraCheck: The rice in the pan
steps.videoShot: Rice sliding from the sieve into the pan.

steps.title: Sauté the rice gently
steps.text: Fold the rice gently from the bottom on medium heat so every grain is coated in ghee.
steps.tip: Fold, do not stir hard. Soaked grains are soft and break easily.
steps.visualCue: The grains look glossy and dry, with no wet patches, and smell lightly toasted.
steps.cameraCheck: Glossy grains in the pan
steps.videoShot: The spatula lifting and folding the rice.

steps.title: Add the water and salt
steps.text: Pour in the 170 ml water and add ¼ tsp (1.5 g) salt. Stir gently once.
steps.tip: Taste the water. It should taste lightly salty, like mild soup.
steps.visualCue: The water just covers the rice by about 0.5 cm.
steps.cameraCheck: The rice under water in the pan
steps.videoShot: Water poured in, salt sprinkled.

steps.title: Bring to a boil
steps.text: Raise the heat to high. Do not cover yet.
steps.visualCue: Bubbles all over the surface and a rolling boil.
steps.cameraCheck: The boiling pan
steps.videoShot: Bubbles breaking across the surface.

steps.title: Simmer until the surface water is gone
steps.text: Lower to medium and let it bubble, uncovered, without stirring.
steps.visualCue: The water level drops below the rice and small steam holes ("craters") appear on the surface.
steps.cameraCheck: The rice surface with steam holes
steps.videoShot: Close-up of steam escaping through holes in the rice.

steps.title: Cover and cook on low
steps.text: Turn the flame to the lowest setting and cover tightly.
steps.tip: Do not lift the lid during these 10 minutes. The steam does the cooking.
steps.visualCue: A faint, steady steam sound; no loud sizzling.
steps.cameraCheck: The covered pan on the lowest flame
steps.videoShot: The lid going on and the knob turned down.

steps.title: Check one grain
steps.text: Lift the lid, take one grain from the top and press it between your fingers.
steps.tip: Still hard? Sprinkle 1–2 tbsp hot water, cover and cook 2–3 min more on low.
steps.visualCue: The grain is soft all the way through, with no hard white centre, and no water is left at the bottom when you tilt the pan.
steps.cameraCheck: A pressed grain on your fingertip
steps.videoShot: Fingers squashing a cooked grain.

steps.title: Rest the rice
steps.text: Switch off the heat and keep the lid on.
steps.visualCue: Grains firm up and stand upright.
steps.cameraCheck: The covered pan off the flame
steps.videoShot: The flame turned off, a timer set to 5 min.

steps.title: Fluff the rice
steps.text: Remove the lid and gently lift and separate the grains with a fork from the sides towards the centre.
steps.tip: Pick out the bay leaf, cloves and cardamom now if you do not want to bite into them.
steps.visualCue: Long, separate, fluffy grains with cumin seeds dotted through.
steps.cameraCheck: The fluffed rice in the pan
steps.videoShot: The fork lifting airy grains.

steps.title: Garnish and serve
steps.text: Sprinkle the chopped coriander and fold once.
steps.visualCue: White rice with brown cumin and green coriander flecks
steps.cameraCheck: The served plate
steps.videoShot: Coriander falling onto the rice, then a slow pan across the plate.

reasons: it is not fried, the home version uses only 1½ tsp ghee, and sodium is moderate (about 590 mg). But it is mostly refined white rice: low in protein (about 6 g) and fibre (about 1.4 g), with no vegetables, so on its own it is a carb side, not a balanced meal. Restaurant versions often finish with an extra spoon of ghee or butter (Tarla Dalal's restaurant-style recipe adds butter at the end), use more salt, and serve a larger portion (often 100 g+ raw rice), which can push it past 450–500 kcal.

researchRating.basis: jeera rice is one of the most widely cooked and ordered Indian rice sides; recipe writers describe it as a restaurant and dhaba bestseller, and recipe pages score high (Hebbar's Kitchen 5/5 from 296 votes; Holy Cow Vegan 5/5 from 20 votes; Whisk Affair 4.22/5 from 19 votes). It loses points because it is seen as a simple supporting dish rather than a star, and reviewers note that it is easy to end up with mushy or bland rice.

storage: Cool the rice quickly (spread it on a plate) and refrigerate in an airtight box within 1 hour of cooking; cooked rice can carry *Bacillus cereus* spores, which multiply if it sits warm at room temperature. Keeps in the fridge for 1–2 days (up to 3 at most). Freezer: yes, flattened in a zip bag or box for up to 1 month. Reheat only once: sprinkle 1–2 tsp water and microwave covered for 1–2 min, stirring halfway, or steam in a covered pan on low heat for 3–4 min, until piping hot throughout.
leftoverRemix: Jeera rice tikki. Mash 1 cup cold leftover jeera rice with 1 small boiled potato, 2 tbsp besan, a pinch of chilli powder, chopped onion and coriander. Shape into 4 small flat patties and shallow-fry on a tawa with 1 tsp oil for 2–3 min per side until golden and crisp. Serve with green chutney. (Quick alternative: a lemon-peanut "jeera-lemon rice" by tossing the rice with a mustard-seed, peanut and curry-leaf tadka and a squeeze of lemon.)
burnOff: about 5.0 km of running (348 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 7 km of brisk walking (about 1 hr 25 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.). With a bowl of dal (about 525 kcal in total): about 7.5 km running or 10.5 km walking (est.).
